prompt: Stage 4-2, augment taken, level 8 with 58 gold and 68 HP, 1-loss streak, losing about 10 HP a round. Your 4-cost carry and 4-cost tank are both 1-star; three copies of the carry are out on other boards. Before you press D you set the floor. What is it?

options.label: Floor at 20: roll 38 gold, nineteen shops, buying every copy of both; if it misses you still have interest, income and a second attempt at 4-5
Roll to 0: every gold raises the hit chance and 68 HP can absorb the misses
Floor at 40: roll 18 gold to keep 4 interest, and hold for 4-5 if it misses

explanation:
The floor is set by what the leftover gold has to do, and at 68 HP it has to buy you options. Six of your carry's 10 copies are in the pool and the 4-cost tier is around 125 copies after the lobby's boards, so one level-8 slot shows your carry about 1.4% of the time and one shop about 7%. Nineteen shops hit at least one copy roughly 75% of the time; twenty-nine shops, rolling to 0, about 88%. The extra 20 gold buys thirteen points of hit chance.

At 0 you earn 5 next round and no interest; a miss leaves you 1-star with no way to level, pivot or roll again before 5-1. At 20 you earn 7, sit near 27 at 4-3 and 35 at 4-5, a second rolldown of the same size. Two 75% attempts beat one 88% attempt.

The floor of 40 fails the other way: nine shops is a sample, not a rolldown, and the 4 interest it protects is worth less than the 25 points of hit chance it gives up.
principle: Set the floor from what the leftover gold has to do; at healthy HP it has to buy you a second attempt.
commonMistake: Rolling to 0 at 68 HP 'because the target matters', then sitting at 5 gold a round with the same 1-star carry.
hint: Compare the hit chance of 19 shops with 29, then ask what 20 gold does for you at 4-3 and 4-5 if the rolldown misses.
